Prompt:
The rate at which a liquid cools is proportional to the difference between its temperature and the temperature of its surroundings. Let [MATH: T(t)] be the temperature of the liquid in degrees Celsius, and let [MATH: t > 0] be the time in minutes. If the temperature of the surroundings is [MATH: 25^{∘}C,] which differential equation could be used to model the temperature of the liquid? Assume that [MATH: k > 0] is a constant of proportionality.

Choices:
a. [MATH: T^{′}(t) = kT(T − 25)]
b. [MATH: T^{′}(t) = kT(T + 25)]
c. [MATH: T^{′}(t) = − kT(T − 25)]
d. [MATH: T^{′}(t) = k(T − 25)]
e. [MATH: T^{′}(t) = − k(T − 25)]
